mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE increases above 0.3pp for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of four consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on overall market returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of six consecutive months where HOUST remains below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over a three-month window indicates firms are hiring while the unemployment rate paradoxically rises due to labor force re-entry, suggesting structural labor market shifts that temporarily depress earnings and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods where PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized growth in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 4% for two consecutive quarters signals robust household demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 4% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of two consecutive quarters with GDPC1 growth exceeding 4% annually.
